questions.question: Relative to an origin O, the points A and B have position vectors (2, -1, 4) and (5, 3, -8). The distance AB is: A 5, B 13, C 19, D 169.
steps: A ignores the z component (sqrt(9 + 16)); C adds the three components 3 + 4 + 12; D leaves out the square root.

questions.question: A unit vector in the direction of 2i - 3j + 6k is: A (2i - 3j + 6k)/11, B (2i - 3j + 6k)/49, C (2i + 3j + 6k)/7, D (2i - 3j + 6k)/7.
steps: A unit vector is the vector divided by its magnitude: (2i - 3j + 6k)/7.
A divides by 2 + 3 + 6 = 11; B divides by the square of the magnitude (no square root); C has the wrong sign for the j component.

questions.question: Relative to an origin O, the points A, B and C have position vectors (1, 2, -3), (4, -1, 3) and (6, -3, 7) respectively. Show that A, B and C are collinear and find the ratio AB : BC.
questions.answer: AB = (3, -3, 6) and BC = (2, -2, 4) are parallel, so A, B, C are collinear; AB : BC = 3 : 2
steps: BC = (2/3)AB, so AB and BC are parallel; they share the point B, so A, B and C lie on a straight line.

questions.question: Relative to an origin O, the points A and B have position vectors 3i - 2j + k and 8i + 3j - 4k respectively. The point P lies on AB such that AP : PB = 2 : 3. Find the position vector of P.

A ship S moves with constant velocity (8i + 6j) km h^-1, where i and j are unit vectors due east and due north respectively. At 12:00 the position vector of S relative to a fixed point O is (-12i + 5j) km. Find the time at which S is due north of O, and the distance of S from O at that time.
steps: At t hours after 12:00 the position vector is r = (-12 + 8t)i + (5 + 6t)j.
S is due north of O when the i component is zero: -12 + 8t = 0, so t = 1.5.
When t = 1.5, r = (5 + 9)j = 14j, so S is 14 km from O.

questions.question: Two boats, P and Q, move with constant velocities. Relative to a fixed point O, the velocity of P is (3i - 2j) km h^-1 and the velocity of Q is (-i + j) km h^-1, where i and j are unit vectors due east and due north respectively. At time t = 0 the position vectors of P and Q are (2i + 5j) km and (10i - 3j) km respectively. Find the speed of P.
steps: Speed = magnitude of the velocity = sqrt(3^2 + (-2)^2).

questions.question: Two boats, P and Q, move with constant velocities. Relative to a fixed point O, the velocity of P is (3i - 2j) km h^-1 and the velocity of Q is (-i + j) km h^-1, where i and j are unit vectors due east and due north respectively. At time t = 0 the position vectors of P and Q are (2i + 5j) km and (10i - 3j) km respectively. Show that, at time t hours, the vector PQ is [(8 - 4t)i + (3t - 8)j] km.
steps: Position of Q: r_Q = (10 - t)i + (-3 + t)j.

questions.question: Two boats, P and Q, move with constant velocities. Relative to a fixed point O, the velocity of P is (3i - 2j) km h^-1 and the velocity of Q is (-i + j) km h^-1, where i and j are unit vectors due east and due north respectively. At time t = 0 the position vectors of P and Q are (2i + 5j) km and (10i - 3j) km respectively. Find the bearing of Q from P at time t = 0.
steps: At t = 0, PQ = 8i - 8j: Q is 8 km east and 8 km south of P.
Q is south-east of P, at 45 degrees below east.

questions.question: Two boats, P and Q, move with constant velocities. Relative to a fixed point O, the velocity of P is (3i - 2j) km h^-1 and the velocity of Q is (-i + j) km h^-1, where i and j are unit vectors due east and due north respectively. At time t = 0 the position vectors of P and Q are (2i + 5j) km and (10i - 3j) km respectively. At time t hours, PQ = [(8 - 4t)i + (3t - 8)j] km. Find the least distance between P and Q in the subsequent motion.
steps: Minimum when d/dt(|PQ|^2) = 50t - 112 = 0, so t = 2.24 h (or complete the square: 25(t - 2.24)^2 + 2.56).

questions.question: The scalar product of the vectors a = 2i - j + 3k and b = i + 4j - 2k is: A -8, B 0, C 4, D 12.
steps: B comes from a sign slip on the j term (2 + 4 - 6) and C from a sign slip on the k term (2 - 4 + 6).
D comes from ignoring all the negative signs (2 + 4 + 6).

questions.question: Two lines have direction vectors (1, 2, 2) and (2, 3, 6). The acute angle between the lines is: A 17.8 degrees, B 68.7 degrees, C 72.2 degrees, D 90 degrees.
steps: The magnitudes are sqrt(1 + 4 + 4) = 3 and sqrt(4 + 9 + 36) = 7, so cos theta = 20/21 and theta = 17.8 degrees.
C is 90 - 17.8, from using sin instead of cos; B uses 1 + 2 + 2 and 2 + 3 + 6 as the magnitudes (cos theta = 20/55); D would need a zero scalar product.

questions.question: Relative to an origin O, the points A, B and C have coordinates (2, -1, 3), (5, 1, 1) and (4, -3, 6) respectively. Find the size of angle BAC, giving your answer in degrees to 1 decimal place.
steps: Angle BAC = 103.6 degrees (1 d.p.), which is obtuse because the scalar product is negative.

questions.question: Relative to an origin O, the points A, B and C have coordinates (0, 1, 2), (2, 3, 3) and (3, 1, 5) respectively. Show that angle ABC = 90 degrees and find the area of triangle ABC.
questions.answer: BA . BC = 0, so angle ABC = 90 degrees; area = 9/2
steps: BA . BC = -2 + 4 - 2 = 0, so BA is perpendicular to BC and angle ABC = 90 degrees.

questions.question: The vectors a = c i + 2j + k and b = i + j + 2k, where c is a constant, are such that the angle between a and b is 60 degrees. Find the possible values of c.
steps: c = 17 or c = -1; both make c + 4 positive, so squaring has not introduced an extra solution.

questions.question: Relative to an origin O, the points A, B and C have coordinates (1, 2, 0), (4, 6, 12) and (1, 5, 4) respectively. Find the lengths AB and AC.
Relative to an origin O, the points A, B and C have coordinates (1, 2, 0), (4, 6, 12) and (1, 5, 4) respectively. Given that AB = 13 and AC = 5, show that cos(angle BAC) = 12/13.

Relative to an origin O, the points A, B and C have coordinates (1, 2, 0), (4, 6, 12) and (1, 5, 4) respectively. Given that AB = 13, AC = 5 and cos(angle BAC) = 12/13, find the exact area of triangle ABC.
steps: Angle BAC is acute, so sin(BAC) = sqrt(1 - (12/13)^2) = sqrt(25/169) = 5/13.

questions.question: Relative to an origin O, the points A, B and C have coordinates (1, 2, 0), (4, 6, 12) and (1, 5, 4) respectively. The area of triangle ABC is 25/2 and AB = 13. Hence find the shortest distance from C to the line through A and B, giving your answer to 3 significant figures.
steps: Take AB as the base of the triangle: area = (1/2) x 13 x h = 25/2.

questions.question: Which of the following is a direction vector of the line through the points (1, 2, -3) and (5, -2, 5)? A 6i + 2k, B 4i + 4j + 8k, C i - j + 2k, D -4i - 4j + 8k.
steps: Any non-zero multiple of this is a direction vector: (4, -4, 8) = 4(1, -1, 2), so i - j + 2k.
A is the sum of the two position vectors, not their difference; B has a sign error in the j component and D has a sign error in the i component.

questions.question: Line l1 has equation r = (1, 2, 0) + s(2, 1, -1) and line l2 has equation r = (0, 3, 1) + t(4, 2, -2). Which statement is correct? A l1 and l2 intersect at exactly one point, B l1 and l2 are parallel and distinct, C l1 and l2 are the same line, D l1 and l2 are skew.
steps: (4, 2, -2) = 2(2, 1, -1), so the direction vectors are parallel; the lines cannot intersect at exactly one point (A) and cannot be skew (D).
Test whether (0, 3, 1) lies on l1: x gives 1 + 2s = 0, so s = -1/2, but then y = 2 - 1/2 = 3/2, not 3.
(0, 3, 1) is not on l1, so the lines are parallel and distinct (B), not the same line (C).

questions.question: The line l passes through the points A(3, -1, 2) and B(5, 3, -4). Find a vector equation of l and show that the point C(9, 11, -16) lies on l.
questions.answer: r = (3, -1, 2) + lambda(2, 4, -6); C lies on l when lambda = 3
steps: A vector equation is r = (3, -1, 2) + lambda(2, 4, -6).
Check the other components with lambda = 3: y = -1 + 12 = 11 and z = 2 - 18 = -16, so C lies on l.

questions.question: The line l1 has equation r = (1, 0, 5) + lambda(2, 1, -1) and the line l2 has equation r = (2, 5, 4) + mu(3, -3, -1), where lambda and mu are parameters. Show that l1 and l2 intersect and find the coordinates of the point of intersection.
steps: Equate components: 1 + 2 lambda = 2 + 3 mu (1); lambda = 5 - 3 mu (2); 5 - lambda = 4 - mu (3).
Substitute (2) into (1): 1 + 10 - 6 mu = 2 + 3 mu, so mu = 1 and lambda = 2.
Check (3): 5 - 2 = 3 and 4 - 1 = 3, so all three equations are satisfied and the lines intersect.
With lambda = 2 in l1, the point is (1 + 4, 0 + 2, 5 - 2) = (5, 2, 3).

questions.question: The line l1 has equation r = (2, 1, -1) + lambda(1, 2, 3) and the line l2 has equation r = (0, 4, 3) + mu(2, -1, 1), where lambda and mu are parameters. Show that l1 and l2 are skew.
questions.answer: The directions are not parallel and the equations are inconsistent, so the lines are skew
steps: The direction vectors (1, 2, 3) and (2, -1, 1) are not multiples of each other, so the lines are not parallel.
Equate components: 2 + lambda = 2 mu (1); 1 + 2 lambda = 4 - mu (2); -1 + 3 lambda = 3 + mu (3).
From (1): lambda = 2 mu - 2. Substitute into (2): 1 + 4 mu - 4 = 4 - mu, so mu = 7/5 and lambda = 4/5.
Check (3): left side = -1 + 12/5 = 7/5, right side = 3 + 7/5 = 22/5. These differ, so the lines do not intersect.
Not parallel and not intersecting, so l1 and l2 are skew.

questions.question: The line l has equation r = (3, 1, 2) + lambda(1, 2, -2), where lambda is a parameter. The point P has coordinates (11, 8, 4). Show that P does not lie on l.
questions.answer: No value of lambda satisfies all three components, so P is not on l
steps: The x component: 3 + lambda = 11 gives lambda = 8.
With lambda = 8 the y component is 1 + 2(8) = 17, which is not 8, so P does not lie on l.

questions.question: The line l has equation r = (3, 1, 2) + lambda(1, 2, -2), where lambda is a parameter. The point P has coordinates (11, 8, 4). The point F lies on l such that PF is perpendicular to l. Find the value of lambda at F and the coordinates of F.
steps: At the point on l with parameter lambda, PF = (3 + lambda - 11, 1 + 2 lambda - 8, 2 - 2 lambda - 4) = (lambda - 8, 2 lambda - 7, -2 lambda - 2).
PF is perpendicular to l, so PF . (1, 2, -2) = 0.

keywords: distance from a point to a line
questions.question: The line l has equation r = (3, 1, 2) + lambda(1, 2, -2), where lambda is a parameter. The point P has coordinates (11, 8, 4). The foot of the perpendicular from P to l is the point F(5, 5, -2). Hence find the shortest distance from P to l.
steps: The shortest distance is the length PF, with PF = (5 - 11, 5 - 8, -2 - 4) = (-6, -3, -6).

questions.question: The line l has equation r = (3, 1, 2) + lambda(1, 2, -2), where lambda is a parameter. The point P has coordinates (11, 8, 4). The foot of the perpendicular from P to l is the point F(5, 5, -2). The point P' is the reflection of P in l. Find the coordinates of P'.
steps: F is the midpoint of PP', so OF = (OP + OP')/2 and OP' = 2 OF - OP.
